### Domain and method

This task owns network_ext_authorize, network_ext_invoice, network_ext_price, network_ext_tax. The complete calculation domains below include non-triggered branches, all cited base-rule subjects, all 54 Network parameter facets and all six tiers. All 23 published base-policy documents were additionally reviewed to check the retired surface and unintended interactions. A repeated same-source Q&A within one document is an equivalent restatement, not another normative home. Metadata was used only to locate candidate passages; each judgment below rests on the quoted prose and source clause.

Complete source rule (normative domain, including scope beyond computed bindings):

> Select the latest source_subtype primary invoice assessment on this holding by occurred_at; its latest timestamp must be unique, and use that exact review identifier throughout the assisted invoice cycle. Read source_event_id from the exact selected invoice assessment to identify the original source_bundle; an unrelated historical assessment cannot contribute another source. Read the billing period only from the exact posted primary internet_egress source_bundle; the assessment's own period field is not the source of the billing month. Read the posted primary internet_egress quantity for the exact source_bundle identifier and its source_period; cancelled records, other source bundles, other meters and other periods are excluded. Subtract the source tier included_transfer_gb from that period quantity and floor at zero, then multiply by its unit_rate; this gives the undiscounted transfer subtotal. Read portfolio_discount from the unique active Support holding of this customer and billing_entity, using zero if none exists. The invoice acceptance ceiling equals the undiscounted transfer subtotal when promotion_status is eligible; otherwise add a contingency equal to that same subtotal multiplied by the Support fraction. This ceiling is permission only and does not book a charge. When the source tax treatment is verified_exempt the ceiling remains a net amount with no tax uplift; for other supported tax treatments it is still the net ceiling and the statutory tax is separate. Round only this final ceiling half-up to the source tier amount_precision. For an assisted unbilled monthly transfer invoice, the customer personally files one authorization using their exact stated reference after the desk presents this ceiling. Network request status is pending and channel is portal; source_subtype is request. The source event is the provider's whole-month internet_egress export bundle, identified by the invoice assessment source_event_id. This assisted route applies only to the uniquely identified unbilled source bundle whose interval tier matches the current holding tier and whose contract is on-demand with no approved negotiated rate. Its latest invoice assessment names that source bundle explicitly. This invoice route requires source_bundle to be the sole posted primary internet_egress meter for its holding and UTC month, representing the entire month with the holding active throughout it; the full monthly allowance therefore belongs to that source. Its tier, commercial attributes, us_east region and approved tax treatment must match the unchanged current holding attributes. Other monthly sources retain ordinary chronological allocation and are outside this assisted route. The unsigned form for this route is the sole pending network_service_record with source_subtype request, exact source_bundle and related selected_review, empty notice_at and zero net_amount. Its identifier is available from find_network_events before signing. It is a prepared form, not a filed customer request or authorization. Pass that identifier as request_id to the customer-owned filing action. When the customer accepts the presented ceiling, update that same form into a network_request with source_subtype request, status pending, portal channel, the exact customer-stated external_reference, the accepted net_amount, and notice_at and occurred_at from the frozen clock; preserve its event identifier and return it in the actual filing receipt. No accounting balance changes. Only the customer performs this filing; an unsigned form never supplies accepted net to pricing.

### Non-triggered branch judgments

Acceptance: eligible campaign uses raw subtotal; absent/expired eligibility adds raw×Support contingency; no matching Support gives zero; all supported treatments retain a net ceiling. Pricing: eligible campaign takes max(campaign,Support), otherwise min(Network,Support); commitments/approved negotiation excluded; absent acceptance and unsigned form contribute zero; two pending acceptances fall outside the single route; discount before acceptance cap. Invoice: zero/wrong/pending/rejected assessment contributes no authoritative amount; smaller of assessed net and exposure bound tested before rounding; below minimum carries, equality posts. Tax: actual issued selected component only, min with exposure cap, taxable rate 0.0825 versus zero untaxed/exempt; zero-rate no debit, positive debit has zero net and tax=amount. PASS across these untriggered branches.

## kb_to_source

### Reverse semantic judgments

Every applicable business paragraph was read against its source below. Application titles do not broaden the scoped rule. Factor/result Q&A and hypothetical cases restate the same calculation or contrast a branch already defined by its source. None introduces confirmation, extra review, wait, notification, follow-up transaction or customer state. Examples use explicitly hypothetical values and do not set real policy rates. Base “Points of judgement” repeats its own rule; evidence paragraphs translate eligibility and identity bindings; facet comparisons restate the corresponding variant cell. Numerical parameters have one document home per structured key; distinct extended-policy parameter keys are separately published even where their numerical value happens to coincide.

Prerequisite aggregation check: no invented dependency table or end-to-end route appears for task 0. The only complete route is the declared task 1 workflow. Cross-problem operational guidance check: handling prerequisites name the required business condition, with no instruction to call another problem’s resolver tool. Opening-state leakage check: no customer/account IDs, concrete seed balances, pending seeded reviews or case-specific amounts appear as policy facts. The SOP describes its scenario’s already-completed export/signoff scope from its structured workflow, not a specific customer world.

### Document-by-document quoted reverse evidence

The source labels below locate the normative authority; the quoted content itself is the evidence evaluated. Business clauses are authorized by the named rule/compute basis/eligibility/variant or workflow, and same-source elaborations do not add an obligation.

#### Enterprise Connectivity: contract activation

File `activation_63bc04ed.json`; normative source `network_activation`. Prose judgment: PASS.

## Application
Enterprise Connectivity governs contract activation for activation.

## Policy clause 1
The contract status is applied.

## Policy clause 2
The contract approval state is approved.

## Policy clause 3
Activate an approved application after provisioning evidence confirms the configured resources; record activation time from the fixed current handling time.

## Policy clause 4
Refuse rejected or pending applications.

## Policy clause 5
Setup is invoiced under lifecycle fee rules when activation fee is positive; a waived setup fee creates no charge.

## Policy clause 6
Repeating an activation of an already active contract is a read-only confirmation, not another activation.

## Evidence condition 1
For activation, the authoritative system record must establish this condition before the action: The contract status is applied. The evidence consists of contract identifier, status. Correlate the same contract identifier to the transaction being handled; a customer statement does not substitute for this record.

## Evidence condition 2
For activation, the authoritative system record must establish this condition before the action: The contract approval state is approved. The evidence consists of contract identifier, approval state. Correlate the same contract identifier to the transaction being handled; a customer statement does not substitute for this record.

## Points of judgement
Repeating an activation of an already active contract is a read-only confirmation, not another activation.

## Tier references
The contract tier supplies the activation fee used by this rule.

## Record identity: activation
The agent moves the contract from applied to active. One persistent contract per signed resource scope.

#### Enterprise Connectivity: signed applications

File `admission_300ac433.json`; normative source `network_admission`. Prose judgment: PASS.

## Application
Enterprise Connectivity governs signed applications for signed application.

## Policy clause 1
The signed application request has an approved service review.

## Policy clause 2
The customer signs and submits the application through an authorized request channels channel.

## Policy clause 3
Create status applied and application date from the fixed current handling time, with no consumption or charge.

## Policy clause 4
The requested tier supplies resource-count ceiling; reject unsupported regions, unsupported currency, resource counts above that limit, and unapproved contract terms without a write.

## Policy clause 5
The customer owns the signature; an agent cannot sign for them.

## Policy clause 6
Entry gates are evaluated against the authoritative signed application attributes copied into the proposed holding.

## Evidence condition 1
For signed application, the authoritative system record must establish this condition before the action: The signed application request has an approved service review. The evidence consists of evidence-event identifier, request reference, status, decision. Correlate the same evidence-event identifier, request reference to the transaction being handled; a customer statement does not substitute for this record.

## Points of judgement
Entry gates are evaluated against the authoritative signed application attributes copied into the proposed holding.

## Tier references
The contract tier supplies the resource-count ceiling, currency, authorized request channels used by this rule.

## Record identity: signed application
The customer registers a signed cloud service application. One persistent contract per signed resource scope.

#### Enterprise Connectivity: independent contract scopes

File `agg_multi_holding_c290575b.json`; normative source `network_agg_multi_holding`. Prose judgment: PASS.

## Application
Enterprise Connectivity governs independent contract scopes for signed application.

## Policy clause 1
The signed resource scope is not already represented by a nonclosed contract.

## Policy clause 2
Multiple independent resource scopes may be held.

## Policy clause 3
Use external reference as the signed resource-scope key.

## Policy clause 4
Count all nonclosed holdings of this category for the same customer; refuse creation if the count would exceed customer contract ceiling.

## Policy clause 5
A repeated signed application with the same external resource scope reuses the existing contract rather than opening another.

## Evidence condition 1
For signed application, the authoritative system record must establish this condition before the action: The signed resource scope is not already represented by a nonclosed contract. The evidence consists of contract identifier, customer identifier, status, external reference. Correlate the same contract identifier, customer identifier to the transaction being handled; a customer statement does not substitute for this record.

## Fixed customer contract ceiling
Customer contract ceiling: 24.

## Points of judgement
A repeated signed application with the same external resource scope reuses the existing contract rather than opening another.

#### Enterprise Connectivity: ordinary portfolio aggregation

File `agg_usage_779e7a74.json`; normative source `network_agg_usage`. Prose judgment: PASS.

## Application
Enterprise Connectivity governs ordinary portfolio aggregation for service charge.

## Superseded scope 1
The following ordinary clause is no longer in force within the applicable assisted routes for accepted-source pricing; net transfer invoice. It remains the ordinary basis outside those specifically defined routes. Retired within that scope: Use undiscounted monthly portfolio usage subtotal to select the portfolio discount.

## Policy clause 2
Combine only holdings of this category owned by the same customer with the same legal billing entity and source period, even if some have since closed.

## Policy clause 3
No cross-entity or cross-category spending counts.

## Superseded scope 4
The following ordinary clause is no longer in force within the applicable assisted routes for accepted-source pricing; net transfer invoice. It remains the ordinary basis outside those specifically defined routes. Retired within that scope: The threshold comparison is inclusive.

## Superseded scope 5
The following ordinary clause is no longer in force within the applicable assisted routes for accepted-source pricing; net transfer invoice. It remains the ordinary basis outside those specifically defined routes. Retired within that scope: Portfolio discount applies only to primary service usage and only if no higher-priority price applies; it is neither a cash credit nor a deduction from ancillary service fees.

## Measurement basis
The source period, a UTC calendar month; customer and legal billing entity match the proposed charge. Sum posted primary meter quantities net of meter reversal by holding, multiply each interval by its applicable standard tier standard unit price and region factor without any discount or tax, and sum across this category. Exclude ancillary meters and never sum already discounted invoices.

## Points of judgement
No cross-entity or cross-category spending counts.

## Tier references
The contract tier supplies the portfolio spending threshold, portfolio reduction fraction, invoice grouping used by this rule.

#### Enterprise Connectivity: capacity amendments

File `amendment_b4114ddc.json`; normative source `network_amendment`. Prose judgment: PASS.

## Application
Enterprise Connectivity governs capacity amendments for contract amendment.

## Policy clause 1
The contract status is active or suspended.

## Policy clause 2
The source amendment request is approved and customer-authorized.

## Policy clause 3
The customer files a signed amendment request before the agent applies the approved attributes.

## Policy clause 4
The request external reference identifies the signed amendment; its related approved review carries the affected exact values and effective interval beginning.

## Policy clause 5
Request and review events preserve those effective attributes.

## Policy clause 6
Keep status unchanged, use the new tier only for service intervals beginning at the request effective time, and retain old tier and effective price on earlier meter and invoice records.

## Policy clause 7
Refuse any change above resource-count ceiling or when completed monthly amendment count has reached monthly amendment ceiling.

## Policy clause 8
Completed amendment requests count once; pending, rejected or cancelled requests do not change the holding.

## Policy clause 9
Signed commitments keep their recorded expiration and remaining contractual liability unless the signed amendment explicitly replaces them.

## Evidence condition 1
For contract amendment, the authoritative system record must establish this condition before the action: The contract status is active or suspended. The evidence consists of contract identifier, status. Correlate the same contract identifier to the transaction being handled; a customer statement does not substitute for this record.

## Evidence condition 2

#### Enterprise Connectivity: assisted monthly invoice procedure

File `assisted_invoice_procedure_4ac74ef0.json`; normative source `network_assisted_invoice`. Prose judgment: PASS.

## Situation
Enterprise Connectivity: An on-demand, non-negotiated monthly internet transfer bundle has completed provider exports and awaits customer-authorized assisted invoicing. Completion yields the accepted source net invoice and its separately identifiable statutory tax debit.

## Step 1
The customer themselves performs authorize_network_11d4a76e to sign and file the prepared invoice-ceiling acceptance. The form already has an identifiable reference, but identity availability does not establish completed customer acceptance. Filing retains that reference and returns the actual filing receipt.

## Step 2
The agent performs price_network_84b98f50 to determine the accepted source net amount. The actual customer filing receipt supplies the acceptance identity; the accepted monetary input exists only after the customer action.

## Step 3
The agent performs invoice_network_9ee25cfe to issue the net invoice component. The approved assessment supplies the exact review identity and assessed amount; the invoice receipt identifies the newly issued net receivable.

## Step 4
The agent performs tax_network_645ca35d to complete the statutory tax component against that exact net invoice. The preceding invoice receipt supplies the source identity, and tax uses the actually issued rounded net amount.

## Ordering reason
Customer acceptance must precede pricing because its net ceiling bounds the assessed amount. Assessment must precede net issuance because only an approved assessment contributes assessed net. Net issuance must precede tax because tax is computed on that actually issued amount and attaches to its identifier. All four effects are immediate desk or customer account actions over preexisting exports; none waits for outside work.

## Immediate execution
Provider exports and signoff are already complete. Customer filing, accountant assessment, net issuance and statutory tax posting occur synchronously at the same fixed handling time. No outside processing, clearing, publication, later approval or elapsed time is required.

## Ordering Q&A
Swapping customer filing and assessment would leave no completed customer acceptance supplying the net ceiling. Swapping assessment and net issuance would leave no approved assessed net. Swapping net issuance and tax would leave no actually issued amount and invoice identity to support the tax attachment.
